title: Dispatch GID 8: Missing Attendant Walks Out of the Impossible Aisle
summary: Her warning is heard at the instant the plate turns toward the wall.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Mabel Crain returned to the Lyceum at 8:17 last night. For almost two minutes after the silvered plate was raised, those inside saw different sights: empty streets, rooms crowded with strangers, and, in our reporter’s view, a theatre filled with people facing away from the stage. The rear passage then became visible to all eleven witnesses present.

Ruth Crain rang the handbell. A figure at the far end of the passage turned toward her. Miss Crain walked forward, stopping twice as the aisle lengthened under her feet. Miss Marsh called for the plate to be turned. At that moment the familiar voice cried, “Turn it off.” Halden swung the plate to the wall. Miss Crain stumbled between the two real rows of seats.

The lamp was still burning. Its light fell on bare plaster, and the extra aisle vanished. The unsold chairs cooled within minutes. Miss Crain identified her sister and said she believed the second demonstration had begun that morning. She says she had walked for perhaps an hour among passages opening into other people’s scenes.

Asked about the warning, she said she had shouted it when she saw the second audience approaching the aisle. She could not say how the words reached the earlier demonstrations. Dr. Saye has confirmed that the last cry matches the two recordings in phrasing and voice, though their background sounds differ.
Miss Crain is resting with her family. Dr. Halden has placed the covered plate in the Institute’s custody. The Lyceum will remain closed while Inspector Voss checks its walls and passages.
